chapter: Decca, Cow Cow Blues and royalties
title: Royalty quarrels with Sidney Bechet and Jimmy Rushing
summary: He describes how he and Jimmy Rushing fell out over money from 'Leave Me' and 'How You Want Your Lovin' Done'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And so does BMI. And so does the union, but they, they, you know,...but I made a lot of records and got nothing. Absolutely nothing. Well I did a thing with Sidney Bechet. I wrote the tune; I said, "Sidney, man, you got half of it.." you know, I'm not liberal. I wrote Same with Jimmy Rushing. /"Leave Me," and "How You Want Your Lovin' Done" on Vanguard. Jimmy and I fell out about those two tunes because...well, what happened was we were going to become a team and Steve Allen wanted us to do a show, you know, wanted to do the tune. So, well we were partners on the songs, we got half the money on the songs...you know, we were going to be partners. Well they only gave me two hundred and ninety dollars for playing the music and gave him six hundred and fifty for singing it. But we were a team, so I said, "Jimmy, it's no more than fair to divide the money." And oh, we had some big thing at the union and I'm amazing, you know, and he's amazing, and it became a big mess...a Masonic matter, a big fraternal...you know what I mean,

almost a lodge meeting. And Cliff Grover said, "Well, Jimmy, if you and Sammy were friends when you had nothing, and when you got something you shared together, and then when you get a little more you want it all, that's not fair." But this is the way we , you know what I mean, this is the way we ' . So that's why I try to stay away from writing any songs for anybody, you know what I mean, I do my own thing.
